newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's biggest hotel in shares, bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Malta's biggest hotel in shares, bond issue.

text.p: Malta's AX leisure and construction group said on Tuesday it was issuing 3.0 million Maltese pounds ($7.83 million) worth of bonds and two million shares in Malta's biggest hotel, the 482-room four star Suncrest.
Group chairman Angelo Xuereb said the group saw the issues as an alternative way to raise finance due to the large number of projects it has in hand.
The projects include a large five-star hotel at the heart of Malta, another hotel in fashionable Sliema and a private hospital.
The two million ordinary shares will be on offer at 75 cents each while the bonds will have an annual interest of 8.25 per cent, subject to approval by the authorities.
The shares will mature at between eight and 10 years in a deal which Xuereb said had already attracted overseas interest.
Suncrest Hotels PLC will raise 4.5 million pounds through the issue -- 1.5 million pounds from the shares and 3.0 million pounds from the bonds.
Money from the shares will go straight to the AX Group which is selling 20 per cent of its shareholding in the Suncrest.
Out of the bond money one million pounds will be used by the hotel for a two-year refurbishment programme with another one million pounds being used to refinance the company's long term loans.
Of the remaining million, half will go to the group's hospitality ventures while the remainder will be used to repay the shareholder's loan.

The Suncrest opened nine years ago and turnover and profits peaked in 1994 at 4.0 million pounds and 1.0 million pounds respectively. Although that slipped to 3.6 million pounds and 800,000 pounds last year, the company is expecting 1997 to again reach the 1994 levels.
The Suncrest is the first tourism-related company to go public. Applications open between March 17 and 22 with the allocations being decided on March 27.
Dealings on the Malta stock exchange will start on April 16. ($1 = 0.38 cents)
